primaryConstraint: There is ZERO Indonesian randomised wording experiments on adult men in the entire corpus of 14 documents.

tier1.title: Zero Indonesian Randomized Wording Experiments
tier1.impact: Blocks confident copywriting: all wording recommendations remain deductive hypotheses.
tier1.solution: Run 2x2 factorial online message tests manipulating pronoun and gender framing.

tier1.title: Absence of Behavioral Outcomes for Men
tier1.impact: Campaigns celebrate literacy/attitude shifts that completely fail to translate into actual help-seeking.
tier1.solution: Track verifiable behavioral conversions (clicks to book, attendance, hotline calls).

tier1.title: Response-Cost Mechanism is Unoperationalized
tier1.impact: Most consistent cross-domain finding (6 of 7 domains) lacks a formal psychometric scale.
tier1.solution: Develop and validate a formal Social Exposure & Response Cost inventory for men.

tier1.title: Severe Geographic and Demographic Sampling Skew
tier1.impact: Findings are heavily Javanese, Muslim, urban, and student-skewed.
tier1.solution: Targeted research in eastern Indonesia, Sumatra, and working-class informal labor sectors.

tier2.title: Intervention Component Bundling
tier2.impact: Cannot tell if setting, imagery, facilitator, or wording caused success in RCTs like FFIT or Man Therapy.

tier2.title: Lack of Male vs Female Comparative Controls
tier2.impact: Persuasion effects working on men are assumed to be male-specific without female testing.

tier2.title: Accommodation vs Expansion Untested Long-Term
tier2.impact: Unresolved tension: does framing help-seeking as 'strength' reinforce the toxic norm that caused stigma?
